about: Reusable proof moves. A proof names the moves it makes (mechanisms); a move connects separate proofs without merging their steps. Each slogan names the object and the action, in ASD-STE100.

mechanisms.name: Finite subcover
mechanisms.slogan: Cover the space by open sets and keep finitely many of them.
mechanisms.description: Compactness turns a local property, true near each point, into a global one through a finite subcover.

mechanisms.name: Local to global
mechanisms.slogan: Prove the property near each point, then join the local results.
mechanisms.description: A local statement extends to the whole space by a cover, a partition of unity, a connectedness argument or a finite subcover.

mechanisms.name: Continuous image
mechanisms.slogan: Push the set forward by the continuous map and keep its property.
mechanisms.description: Continuous maps send compact sets to compact sets and connected sets to connected sets.

mechanisms.name: Least upper bound
mechanisms.slogan: Take the supremum of the set and show that it has the property.
mechanisms.description: Completeness of the real numbers gives a supremum; the proof shows that it is the required point or value.

mechanisms.name: Nested intervals and bisection
mechanisms.slogan: Halve the interval again and again, and keep the half with the property.
mechanisms.description: A decreasing sequence of closed bounded intervals has a common point; bisection produces such a sequence.

mechanisms.name: Convergent subsequence
mechanisms.slogan: Extract a subsequence that converges, then pass to its limit.
mechanisms.description: Sequential compactness, or a diagonal argument, gives a convergent subsequence whose limit has the required property.

mechanisms.name: Diagonal argument
mechanisms.slogan: Build an object that differs from the n-th listed object at place n.
mechanisms.description: Cantor's diagonal construction shows non-enumerability, undecidability or the existence of a subsequence that works for countably many conditions.

mechanisms.name: Epsilon-delta estimate
mechanisms.slogan: Fix a tolerance, then choose a closeness that gives it.
mechanisms.description: A limit or continuity statement is proved by an explicit choice of delta, or N, for each epsilon.

mechanisms.name: Three-epsilon split
mechanisms.slogan: Split the distance into three small parts and bound each part.
mechanisms.description: The triangle inequality splits an error into terms that a uniform approximation, a fixed approximation and continuity each make small.

mechanisms.name: Triangle inequality chain
mechanisms.slogan: Insert intermediate points and add the distances.
mechanisms.description: An estimate of a distance follows from the sum of the distances through intermediate points.

mechanisms.name: Cauchy sequence and completeness
mechanisms.slogan: Show that the sequence is Cauchy, then take its limit in the complete space.
mechanisms.description: Completeness gives a limit for every Cauchy sequence; the proof builds a Cauchy sequence of approximations.

mechanisms.name: Iteration of a contraction
mechanisms.slogan: Apply the map again and again from a start point, and take the limit.
mechanisms.description: Iterates of a contraction form a Cauchy sequence whose limit is the unique fixed point.

mechanisms.name: Extremum on a compact set
mechanisms.slogan: Minimize the quantity over a compact set, then study the minimizer.
mechanisms.description: A continuous function on a nonempty compact set attains its minimum; the minimizer then supplies the required object.

mechanisms.name: Baire category
mechanisms.slogan: Write the complete space as a countable union, then find a piece with interior.
mechanisms.description: In a complete metric space a countable union of closed sets with empty interior has empty interior.

mechanisms.name: Uniform limit exchange
mechanisms.slogan: Approximate uniformly, then pass the property to the limit.
mechanisms.description: Uniform convergence lets continuity, integrals or derivatives pass to the limit function.

mechanisms.name: Dominated convergence
mechanisms.slogan: Bound the functions by one integrable function, then exchange the limit and the integral.
mechanisms.description: Pointwise convergence with an integrable bound gives convergence of the integrals.

mechanisms.name: Monotone limit
mechanisms.slogan: Show that the sequence is monotone and bounded, then take its limit.
mechanisms.description: A bounded monotone sequence of reals converges; monotone convergence does the same for integrals.

mechanisms.name: Telescoping sum
mechanisms.slogan: Write each term as a difference and cancel the inner terms.
mechanisms.description: A sum of consecutive differences equals the difference of its end terms.

mechanisms.name: Integrate the derivative
mechanisms.slogan: Write the change as the integral of the derivative.
mechanisms.description: The fundamental theorem of calculus turns a difference of values into an integral of a rate.

mechanisms.name: Mean value point
mechanisms.slogan: Find a point where the derivative equals the average rate.
mechanisms.description: Rolle's theorem or the mean value theorem gives an intermediate point that controls a difference.

mechanisms.name: Taylor expansion with remainder
mechanisms.slogan: Expand the function to finite order and bound the remainder.
mechanisms.description: A Taylor polynomial with an explicit remainder gives local estimates.

mechanisms.name: Convexity inequality
mechanisms.slogan: Compare the function with its chord or tangent line.
mechanisms.description: Convexity gives Jensen-type inequalities: the value at a mean is at most the mean of the values.

mechanisms.name: Cauchy-Schwarz bound
mechanisms.slogan: Pair the two factors in an inner product and bound the product by the norms.
mechanisms.description: The Cauchy-Schwarz inequality bounds a sum or an integral of products.

mechanisms.name: Orthogonal projection
mechanisms.slogan: Project the vector onto the closed subspace and study the error.
mechanisms.description: In a Hilbert space the nearest point of a closed convex set exists, and the error is orthogonal to a subspace.

mechanisms.name: Extension of a linear map
mechanisms.slogan: Define the map on a subspace, then extend it with control of its size.
mechanisms.description: Hahn-Banach, density or a basis extends a linear map from a subspace to the whole space.

mechanisms.name: Extension by density
mechanisms.slogan: Prove the statement on a dense set, then pass to limits.
mechanisms.description: A continuous statement true on a dense subset is true everywhere.

mechanisms.name: Change of variables
mechanisms.slogan: Replace the variable by a new one and transform the measure.
mechanisms.description: A substitution simplifies an integral or a sum; the Jacobian or a bijection controls the change.

mechanisms.name: Exchange of summation or integration
mechanisms.slogan: Swap the order of the two sums or integrals.
mechanisms.description: Fubini or Tonelli exchanges iterated integrals or sums under integrability or positivity.

mechanisms.name: Generating function
mechanisms.slogan: Encode the sequence as power-series coefficients and compute with the series.
mechanisms.description: A generating function turns a recurrence or a counting problem into algebra on series.

mechanisms.name: Fourier or characteristic function
mechanisms.slogan: Transform the object to frequencies and study the transform.
mechanisms.description: A Fourier transform or characteristic function turns convolution into products and convergence of laws into pointwise convergence.

mechanisms.name: Contour integration
mechanisms.slogan: Integrate the holomorphic function around a closed path and read the result.
mechanisms.description: Cauchy's theorem, the integral formula or residues give values, estimates or zeros from contour integrals.

mechanisms.name: Maximum principle
mechanisms.slogan: Find where the function is largest and show that the maximum is on the boundary.
mechanisms.description: Harmonic or holomorphic functions, and solutions of elliptic equations, have no interior maximum unless constant.

mechanisms.name: Identity theorem and continuation
mechanisms.slogan: Show that two analytic functions agree on a set with a limit point, then join them.
mechanisms.description: Analytic functions that agree near a point agree on the connected domain.

mechanisms.name: Induction on a natural number
mechanisms.slogan: Prove the base case, then derive case n+1 from case n.
mechanisms.description: A statement about all natural numbers follows from a base case and a step.

mechanisms.name: Strong induction or minimal counterexample
mechanisms.slogan: Assume all smaller cases, then prove the next case.
mechanisms.description: Strong induction, or a minimal counterexample, uses every smaller case of the statement.

mechanisms.name: Structural induction
mechanisms.slogan: Prove the property for the base objects and for each construction rule.
mechanisms.description: Induction over terms, formulas, trees or inductive types.

mechanisms.name: Least element
mechanisms.slogan: Take the least element of the set and derive a contradiction or the result.
mechanisms.description: Every nonempty set of natural numbers, or of ordinals, has a least element.

mechanisms.name: Infinite descent
mechanisms.slogan: Build a smaller solution from each solution until no smaller one can exist.
mechanisms.description: A strictly decreasing infinite sequence of natural numbers cannot exist.

mechanisms.name: Contradiction
mechanisms.slogan: Assume the negation and derive a false statement.
mechanisms.description: The statement follows because its negation implies a contradiction.

mechanisms.name: Contrapositive
mechanisms.slogan: Prove that the failure of the conclusion makes a hypothesis fail.
mechanisms.description: The proof shows not-B implies not-A instead of A implies B.

mechanisms.name: Case analysis
mechanisms.slogan: Split the situation into cases and treat each case.
mechanisms.description: A finite division into exhaustive cases, each with its own argument.

mechanisms.name: Extremal choice
mechanisms.slogan: Choose the largest or smallest object of its kind and study it.
mechanisms.description: An object that maximizes or minimizes a quantity has extra properties that the proof uses.

mechanisms.name: Pigeonhole
mechanisms.slogan: Put more objects than boxes into the boxes and find a shared box.
mechanisms.description: If n objects go into fewer than n boxes, some box holds two objects; averages give the general form.

mechanisms.name: Double counting
mechanisms.slogan: Count one set of pairs in two ways and equate the counts.
mechanisms.description: Two counts of the same finite set give an identity or an inequality.

mechanisms.name: Bijection
mechanisms.slogan: Match the two sets one to one and compare their sizes.
mechanisms.description: An explicit bijection proves that two finite sets have the same size, or transfers structure.

mechanisms.name: Inclusion-exclusion
mechanisms.slogan: Add the sizes of the sets, then correct the overlaps with alternating signs.
mechanisms.description: The size of a union is an alternating sum over intersections.

mechanisms.name: Averaging
mechanisms.slogan: Compute the average, then find one object at least as good as the average.
mechanisms.description: Some element is at least the mean, and some is at most the mean.

mechanisms.name: Probabilistic method
mechanisms.slogan: Choose the object at random and show a positive chance of success.
mechanisms.description: A random construction with positive success probability proves existence.

mechanisms.name: Linearity of expectation
mechanisms.slogan: Write the count as a sum of indicators and add their expectations.
mechanisms.description: Expectation is additive even for dependent variables.

mechanisms.name: Union bound
mechanisms.slogan: Bound the chance of any bad event by the sum of their chances.
mechanisms.description: The probability of a union is at most the sum of the probabilities.

mechanisms.name: Exponential moment bound
mechanisms.slogan: Bound the exponential moment, then apply Markov's inequality to it.
mechanisms.description: Chernoff-type bounds control tails through the moment generating function.

mechanisms.name: Martingale argument
mechanisms.slogan: Build a martingale from the process and use its stopping or convergence property.
mechanisms.description: Optional stopping, martingale convergence or martingale differences control the process.

mechanisms.name: Coupling
mechanisms.slogan: Put the two random objects on one probability space and compare them pointwise.
mechanisms.description: A joint construction of two laws gives comparisons and distances between them.

mechanisms.name: Borel-Cantelli
mechanisms.slogan: Sum the probabilities of the events and conclude that only finitely many occur.
mechanisms.description: A convergent sum of probabilities implies that almost surely only finitely many events happen.

mechanisms.name: Symmetry
mechanisms.slogan: Apply the symmetry to the object and compare the two versions.
mechanisms.description: An invariance under a symmetry reduces cases or forces a value.

mechanisms.name: Orbits of a group action
mechanisms.slogan: Let the group act on a set and count the orbits and stabilizers.
mechanisms.description: The orbit-stabilizer theorem and the class equation turn actions into counts.

mechanisms.name: Cosets and index
mechanisms.slogan: Split the group into cosets of the subgroup and count them.
mechanisms.description: Cosets of a subgroup partition the group into blocks of equal size.

mechanisms.name: Quotient
mechanisms.slogan: Divide the object by the relation and work in the quotient.
mechanisms.description: A quotient group, ring, module or space removes the structure that the proof does not need.

mechanisms.name: Kernel and image
mechanisms.slogan: Build a homomorphism and compare its kernel and image.
mechanisms.description: The first isomorphism theorem identifies the image with a quotient by the kernel.

mechanisms.name: Exact sequence and diagram chase
mechanisms.slogan: Put the objects in an exact sequence and chase an element through the diagram.
mechanisms.description: Exactness and commutativity move an element step by step to the required conclusion.

mechanisms.name: Long exact sequence
mechanisms.slogan: Write the long exact sequence of the pair and read the unknown term.
mechanisms.description: A short exact sequence of complexes gives a long exact sequence in (co)homology.

mechanisms.name: Dimension count
mechanisms.slogan: Compare the dimensions of the spaces and conclude.
mechanisms.description: Rank-nullity, a basis count or a degree count forces a space to be nonzero or two spaces to be equal.

mechanisms.name: Eigenvector decomposition
mechanisms.slogan: Find an eigenvector and split the space along it.
mechanisms.description: An eigenvector, an invariant subspace or an orthogonal complement reduces the dimension.

mechanisms.name: Determinant or characteristic polynomial
mechanisms.slogan: Compute the determinant or the characteristic polynomial and read its roots.
mechanisms.description: Determinants detect invertibility; characteristic polynomials give eigenvalues and relations.

mechanisms.name: Row reduction and factorization
mechanisms.slogan: Reduce the matrix by elementary operations to a simple form.
mechanisms.description: Gaussian elimination, Smith normal form or a factorization gives a canonical form.

mechanisms.name: Division with remainder
mechanisms.slogan: Divide by the element and study the remainder.
mechanisms.description: Division with remainder in the integers or polynomials gives Euclid's algorithm and principal ideals.

mechanisms.name: Reduction modulo n
mechanisms.slogan: Reduce the equation modulo a well-chosen number and compare residues.
mechanisms.description: Congruences turn an integer problem into a finite one.

mechanisms.name: Prime factorization
mechanisms.slogan: Write the numbers as products of primes and compare the exponents.
mechanisms.description: Unique factorization reduces divisibility questions to exponent comparisons.

mechanisms.name: Euclidean algorithm
mechanisms.slogan: Replace the pair by the smaller number and the remainder until the remainder is zero.
mechanisms.description: Repeated division finds the greatest common divisor and Bezout coefficients.

mechanisms.name: Degree of a field extension
mechanisms.slogan: Compute the degrees of the extensions and multiply them along the tower.
mechanisms.description: The tower law and minimal polynomials control which numbers lie in which fields.

mechanisms.name: Galois correspondence
mechanisms.slogan: Match subgroups of the Galois group with intermediate fields.
mechanisms.description: The fundamental theorem of Galois theory turns field questions into group questions.

mechanisms.name: Local-global reduction
mechanisms.slogan: Solve the problem at each prime or each point, then combine the local answers.
mechanisms.description: Localization, completion or a Chinese remainder argument assembles a global answer from local ones.

mechanisms.name: Zorn's lemma
mechanisms.slogan: Order the partial objects, check that every chain has a bound, and take a maximal object.
mechanisms.description: A maximal element of a suitable partial order supplies a basis, an ideal, an extension or a choice.

mechanisms.name: Finite satisfiability
mechanisms.slogan: Satisfy every finite part of the theory, then satisfy the whole theory.
mechanisms.description: Compactness in logic, or in a product of finite sets, passes from finite parts to the whole.

mechanisms.name: Coding and self-reference
mechanisms.slogan: Encode the statements as numbers and build a sentence about its own code.
mechanisms.description: Godel numbering and a fixed-point lemma produce self-referential statements.

mechanisms.name: Reduction to a known problem
mechanisms.slogan: Transform an instance of the known problem into an instance of the new problem.
mechanisms.description: A computable or polynomial-time transformation transfers hardness or undecidability.

mechanisms.name: Universal property
mechanisms.slogan: Find the unique map that the universal property gives and compare the objects.
mechanisms.description: Objects defined by a universal property are unique up to unique isomorphism; maps out of them are determined.

mechanisms.name: Yoneda embedding
mechanisms.slogan: Replace the object by the functor it represents and compare the functors.
mechanisms.description: Natural transformations out of a representable functor correspond to elements; objects are determined by their functors of points.

mechanisms.name: Adjunction
mechanisms.slogan: Move the problem across the adjunction and solve it on the other side.
mechanisms.description: A pair of adjoint functors turns maps out of one object into maps into another; left adjoints keep colimits.

mechanisms.name: Functoriality
mechanisms.slogan: Apply the functor to the diagram and read the induced maps.
mechanisms.description: A functor sends a commuting diagram to a commuting diagram; invariants obstruct maps.

mechanisms.name: Homotopy invariance
mechanisms.slogan: Deform the map or the space continuously and keep the invariant.
mechanisms.description: Homotopic maps induce the same map on homotopy-invariant functors such as homology.

mechanisms.name: Lifting to a cover
mechanisms.slogan: Lift the path or the map to the covering space and read its end point.
mechanisms.description: Path lifting and the lifting criterion compute fundamental groups and degrees.

mechanisms.name: Degree or winding number
mechanisms.slogan: Count how many times the map wraps around and compare the counts.
mechanisms.description: Degree or winding number is an integer invariant that forces zeros or fixed points.

mechanisms.name: Euler characteristic count
mechanisms.slogan: Count vertices, edges and faces and take the alternating sum.
mechanisms.description: The alternating sum of cell counts is a topological invariant.

mechanisms.name: Cut and glue
mechanisms.slogan: Cut the space into two simpler pieces and glue their invariants.
mechanisms.description: Mayer-Vietoris or Seifert-van Kampen computes an invariant of a union from the pieces and their overlap.

mechanisms.name: Partition of unity
mechanisms.slogan: Build local objects on charts and glue them with a partition of unity.
mechanisms.description: Smooth partitions of unity glue local functions, metrics or forms into global ones.

mechanisms.name: Boundary integration
mechanisms.slogan: Move the integral from the region to its boundary.
mechanisms.description: Stokes, Green, Gauss or the divergence theorem converts an integral of a derivative into a boundary integral.

mechanisms.name: Curvature comparison
mechanisms.slogan: Compare the space with a model space of constant curvature.
mechanisms.description: Bounds on curvature control lengths, angles and volumes through comparison with model spaces.

mechanisms.name: Variational method
mechanisms.slogan: Minimize an energy and show that the minimizer solves the equation.
mechanisms.description: The minimizer of a functional satisfies its Euler-Lagrange equation.

mechanisms.name: A priori estimate
mechanisms.slogan: Bound the solution by the data before you construct it.
mechanisms.description: Energy estimates, Gronwall or Sobolev inequalities give bounds that pass to limits.

mechanisms.name: Fixed-point theorem
mechanisms.slogan: Write the solution as a fixed point of a map and apply a fixed-point theorem.
mechanisms.description: Banach, Brouwer, Schauder or Kakutani gives a fixed point that is the solution.

mechanisms.name: Approximation by simple objects
mechanisms.slogan: Approximate the object by simpler objects and pass the property to the limit.
mechanisms.description: Polynomials, step functions, finite-rank operators or smooth functions approximate the object.

mechanisms.name: Spectral decomposition
mechanisms.slogan: Decompose the operator into its spectral pieces and treat each piece.
mechanisms.description: Diagonalization, the spectral theorem or a functional calculus reduces an operator to multiplication.

mechanisms.name: Characters and orthogonality
mechanisms.slogan: Compute the characters and use their orthogonality.
mechanisms.description: Characters of representations are orthogonal class functions that decompose representations.

mechanisms.name: Explicit construction
mechanisms.slogan: Write down the object and check its properties one by one.
mechanisms.description: An existence statement proved by an explicit formula or example.

mechanisms.name: Family of examples
mechanisms.slogan: Build a family of examples and compute the quantity for each member.
mechanisms.description: A parametrized family shows sharpness or rules out a stronger statement.

mechanisms.name: Interpolation
mechanisms.slogan: Bound the operator at the two ends and interpolate between them.
mechanisms.description: Riesz-Thorin, Holder or log-convexity bounds an intermediate quantity by the end points.

mechanisms.name: Sieve
mechanisms.slogan: Remove the multiples of each small prime and estimate what remains.
mechanisms.description: Sieves count integers free of small prime factors with controlled error terms.

mechanisms.name: Height and descent
mechanisms.slogan: Measure the size of the points by a height and reduce to finitely many points.
mechanisms.description: Heights with descent show that a group of rational points is finitely generated.

mechanisms.name: Graph traversal
mechanisms.slogan: Walk through the graph from a start vertex and record the vertices you reach.
mechanisms.description: Breadth-first or depth-first search builds trees, paths, components and orderings.

mechanisms.name: Augmenting path
mechanisms.slogan: Find a path that improves the current solution and use it until no path remains.
mechanisms.description: Matchings and flows grow by augmenting paths; the absence of a path certifies optimality.

mechanisms.name: Duality
mechanisms.slogan: Write the dual problem and compare its value with the primal value.
mechanisms.description: Linear-programming, convex or Pontryagin duality gives matching bounds from the other side.

mechanisms.name: Separating hyperplane
mechanisms.slogan: Separate the convex set from the point by a hyperplane.
mechanisms.description: Convex sets are separated by linear functionals, which gives duality and extension results.

mechanisms.name: Algebraic identity
mechanisms.slogan: Expand both sides and compare the terms.
mechanisms.description: A direct computation, expansion or factorization proves an identity.

mechanisms.name: Auxiliary construction
mechanisms.slogan: Add an auxiliary point, line or circle and compare the new figures.
mechanisms.description: A construction in the figure reveals congruent or similar triangles, equal angles or areas.

mechanisms.name: Similar figures
mechanisms.slogan: Find two similar figures and compare corresponding ratios.
mechanisms.description: Similar triangles or a scaling map give equal ratios.

mechanisms.name: Coordinates
mechanisms.slogan: Put the figure in coordinates and compute.
mechanisms.description: Cartesian, complex or barycentric coordinates turn geometry into algebra.

mechanisms.name: Sheaf gluing
mechanisms.slogan: Define the object on an open cover and glue the pieces on the overlaps.
mechanisms.description: Local sections that agree on overlaps glue to a global section; cohomology measures the failure.

mechanisms.name: Spectral sequence
mechanisms.slogan: Filter the complex and compute its homology page by page.
mechanisms.description: A filtration gives a spectral sequence that converges to the homology of the whole.

mechanisms.name: Index computation
mechanisms.slogan: Compute the index from a topological formula instead of from the kernel.
mechanisms.description: Fredholm and index theorems compute an analytic quantity by a topological one.

mechanisms.name: Modularity and automorphic lifting
mechanisms.slogan: Attach a modular or automorphic form to the object and use its properties.
mechanisms.description: Modularity links Galois representations or elliptic curves to modular forms.

mechanisms.name: Cited deep result
mechanisms.slogan: Reduce the statement to a major theorem and cite that theorem.
mechanisms.description: The proof step rests on a long published result that this catalog does not unfold.
